items.title: YaB security CI gate has failed on every run for 7 days: axios 1.17.0 carries an unpatched HIGH prod advisory
items.impact: The one automated advisory gate the SECURITY_POLICY names as bounding exposure to one week is red and has been ignored for nine consecutive runs, so no PR has passed an advisory scan since 2026-07-20.
items.detail: .github/workflows/security.yml:51 runs `pnpm audit --audit-level=high --prod`. That command exits 1 today on GHSA-gcfj-64vw-6mp9 (axios >=1.15.2 <1.18.0, patched >=1.18.0), reached via apps/api > plaid@42.2.0 > axios@1.17.0. `gh run list --workflow=security.yml` shows failure on every run from 2026-07-25T03:34:10Z through 2026-07-27T11:18:09Z (9 runs, main and dependabot branches); the last success was 2026-07-20T11:13:51Z. On the latest main run the vitest and typecheck jobs pass and only the pnpm audit job fails. A second HIGH, GHSA-r28c-9q8g-f849 (postcss <=8.5.17, patched >=8.5.18), shows in the dev-inclusive audit via vite/vitest; it does not fail the --prod gate but is the same one-line remedy.
items.prompt:
In X:\YesAndBudget, clear the two HIGH npm advisories and get the security workflow green.

(1) Reproduce first: run `pnpm audit --audit-level=high --prod` from X:\YesAndBudget and confirm it exits 1 on axios. Then run `pnpm audit --audit-level high` (no --prod) and confirm postcss also shows HIGH. If either no longer reproduces, say so and close the item as refuted rather than editing anything.

(2) package.json already carries a pnpm.overrides block with exactly this pattern ("form-data@>=4.0.0 <4.0.6": ">=4.0.6" and "vite@<6.4.3": ">=6.4.3"), added in v0.14.3 for the same class of transitive advisory. Add two more in the same shape: "axios@<1.18.0": ">=1.18.0" and "postcss@<8.5.18": ">=8.5.18". Do not bump plaid to chase axios; the override is the established pattern here and keeps the Plaid SDK pinned.

(3) pnpm install, then re-run BOTH audit commands and confirm clean at high+.

(4) Run scripts/preship.ps1 (pnpm -r build + pnpm -r test) and confirm green. axios is the transport under apps/api/src/plaid/, so the Plaid tests are the ones that matter.

(5) Release via scripts/release.ps1 as a PATCH, then confirm the security workflow goes green on main with `gh run list --workflow=security.yml --limit 3`. The item is not done until a run on main reports success.

(6) Worth naming in the release message: this sat red for 7 days because nothing in the nightly chain reads CI conclusions. That gap is tracked by bar-raise-2026-07-27-yab-observability-06; do not fix it here.
items.notes: New HIGH from the 2026-07-27 bar-raise. Live breakage: the gate is red now, not a latent risk.

items.title: Nothing in the nightly chain reads GitHub Actions conclusions, so a red CI gate ran unnoticed for 7 days
items.impact: A failing security gate is invisible to every automated review surface; it took a manual gh run list during a bar-raise to notice nine consecutive failures.
items.detail: audit-budget-nightly, handler-audit-nightly, working-tree-scan-nightly and bar-raise-budget all fired on schedule every day from 2026-07-25 to 2026-07-27 and none of them reported the security.yml failures over that window. The routines read the working tree, the canonical docs, the queue and the status JSON, but never the remote CI state. The status JSON has no field for it either.
items.prompt:
In X:\YesAndBudget (and the shared routine that covers it), make a red CI run visible to the nightly chain.

(1) Reproduce: `gh run list --workflow=security.yml --limit 12 --json conclusion,createdAt,headBranch`. Confirm the failure streak is real and current before building anything. If CI is green by the time this is picked up, the gap is still real but re-scope the item to prevention only.

(2) Smallest useful fix: have audit-budget-nightly query the latest conclusion for each workflow on main and write it into X:\YesAndEverything\status\data\Budget.json as a ci block ({workflow, conclusion, url, checkedAt}), so a red gate lands on the dashboard the same night it goes red.

(3) Report a red conclusion as an audit finding in the nightly report, not only as a JSON field, so the bar-raise picks it up as evidence the next morning.

(4) This is a portfolio-shaped gap, not a Budget-only one: every repo with GitHub Actions has it. Do the Budget wiring, then note in the result whether the same step belongs in the shared audit routine template. Do not fan the change out to other repos in this item.
items.notes: Companion to bar-raise-2026-07-27-yab-dependency-04. That item fixes the red gate; this one is why nobody saw it.

items.title: Budget.json non-barRaise fields are stale in four places at once, so the dashboard reads calm while the project is not
items.impact: The dashboard shows Budget as clean-tree, zero-findings and 14 queue items on a day with a dirty tree, a HIGH canonical-audit finding, 20 queue rows and a red CI gate.
items.detail: X:\YesAndEverything\status\data\Budget.json on 2026-07-27: audit.latestReportPath names docs/CANONICAL_AUDIT-2026-07-26.md, which report retention deleted (only CANONICAL_AUDIT-2026-07-27.md is on disk); audit.findings reads high 0 / medium 0 / low 0 while the 2026-07-27 audit found 1 HIGH, 3 MEDIUM and 2 LOW; workTreeClean is true while `git status --porcelain` shows docs/DESIGN.md and docs/SECURITY_POLICY.md modified; workQueueDepth is 14 while the live queue holds 20 Budget rows. These fields are written by scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1 at release time and by nothing else, so they freeze between releases while the bar-raise block updates daily.
items.prompt:
In X:\YesAndBudget, stop the non-barRaise half of Budget.json going stale between releases.

(1) Reproduce: read X:\YesAndEverything\status\data\Budget.json and compare audit.latestReportPath against `ls X:\YesAndBudget\docs\CANONICAL_AUDIT-*.md`, audit.findings against the newest audit report TL;DR, workTreeClean against `git -C X:\YesAndBudget status --porcelain`, and workQueueDepth against the Budget rows in X:\YesAndEverything\.work-queue.json. Confirm all four before changing anything.

(2) The root cause is ownership, not any single wrong value: scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1 owns these fields and only runs on release. Give audit-budget-nightly a dashboard-refresh step that rewrites audit.*, workTreeClean and workQueueDepth from live state each night, the same way the bar-raise block already refreshes daily. Reuse the atomic-write helper at write-dashboard-status.ps1:222-245 and preserve every field it does not own, including the whole barRaise block (see v0.14.11 for what cherry-picking cost).

(3) Retention interacts with this: the pointer names a file the retention policy deletes. Either have the nightly step write the pointer to whatever newest report is actually on disk, or accept that the pointer can name a deleted file and say so in the field. Pick one and write the choice down.

(4) The long-standing finding orchestration-audit-loop-integrity-03 covers the audit-pointer half only. Close it out as part of this if the fix lands.
items.notes: Widened from the pointer-only finding: the same release-only ownership makes three more fields stale.

items.prompt:
YaE HIGH (bar-raise-everything 2026-07-27): eight of the nine project pages carry hand-written status prose that no stamping step ever refreshes, and two of them misdescribe their project on the live public site right now.

ROOT CAUSE: scripts/update-project-pages.mjs supports two markers per page (see its header comment lines 6-10): <!--live:version:Proj-->...<!--/live--> and <!--live:milestone:Proj-->...<!--/live-->. All nine project pages carry the version marker. Only projects/here-be-hordes/index.html carries the milestone marker. So version is refreshed on every deploy and milestone prose is frozen at whatever was typed by hand.

PROVEN LIVE DRIFT (two pages, re-fetch before you start to confirm they are still wrong):
  - projects/budget/index.html:242 pill reads 'M0–M5 shipped' and :307 reads 'M5 shipped (binary-PDF deferred); M6 budgets + goals in progress'. status/data/Budget.json says milestone M6 'Budgets + goals' status=done, completion.pct=100, anchored 2026-06-25. The page is a month behind and understates a finished project.
  - projects/cattery/index.html reads 'Phase one is listings plus messaging - no payments in the loop'. status/data/Cattery.json says 'Phase 2 built (escrow payments, reviews, waitlists, admin tiers); launch-readiness next' at v0.25.1 / 84%. The page says payments do not exist; the project says escrow payments shipped.

ORDER:
  (1) Read projects/here-be-hordes/index.html and copy its milestone-marker shape exactly. It wraps ONLY the short status clause ('The current milestone is M4, Pre-Production Lock'), leaving the rest of the prose hand-written. That is the pattern; do not template the whole paragraph.
  (2) For each of the eight pages (apothecary, brackish-rising, budget, cattery, chains, gnosis, ring, scheduler), identify the one clause that states current status and wrap it in <!--live:milestone:<Proj>-->...<!--/live--> using the SAME project id the status JSON filename uses (Rising not brackish-rising, Hordes not here-be-hordes; see the SLUGS / PUBLIC_COPY maps in scripts/update-project-pages.mjs:25 and :41).
  (3) Fix the Budget and Cattery prose in the same pass so the pre-stamp committed text is not itself wrong.
  (4) Run `node scripts/update-project-pages.mjs` locally and diff. Every one of the nine pages should now show a milestone substitution, not just Hordes.
  (5) FUSE: write these files with the Python atomic-write-with-readback pattern (X:\YesAndChains\tools\safe_write.py), tail-check each one ends with </html>, then release via scripts/release.ps1.
  (6) Verify live: fetch /projects/budget/ and /projects/cattery/ and confirm the milestone text now matches the status JSON. A local diff is not verification; the stamping runs in the Pages workflow.

NOT IN SCOPE: do not port Budget or Scheduler onto the current page template in this item. That is a separate queued item and it is blocked behind the template regaining its h2 headings.

items.prompt: YaE MEDIUM (bar-raise-everything 2026-07-27): four em and en dashes ship on public pages as HTML entities, so every existing voice check misses them. The rule is not being broken by accident, it is being broken invisibly. THE FOUR: - terms/index.html:6 Consultation Terms — yesandeverything.com - budget/index.html:6 YesAndBudget — launcher - projects/budget/index.html:242 M0–M5 shipped - projects/budget/index.html:307 'MVP (M0–M4) shipped May 2026' WHY IT SURVIVED: `grep -c $'\u2014' ` returns 0 on all four, because the character is never in the source. Only a search for the entity forms finds them. ORDER: (1) Replace the two title dashes with a hyphen or a rewording. '404 - yesandeverything' at 404.html:6 is the shape the rest of the site already uses, so match it. (2) Replace the two – range dashes with a plain hyphen ('M0-M5 shipped'). (3) CONFIRM WITH KANE BEFORE TOUCHING terms/index.html. It is the legal page and its wording is deliberate; the title is almost certainly safe to change but a legal surface does not get edited unattended. (4) Extend whatever voice check exists (solo-dev-voice-audit and any grep in the release scripts) to match —, –, — and – alongside the literal characters, otherwise this recurs silently. (5) FUSE: atomic write plus readback, tail-check , release via scripts/release.ps1. NOTE: projects/budget/index.html also carries stale milestone prose and is queued separately for the live:milestone marker work. If both items run in the same session, do them in one edit of that file.

items.impact: Routines complete work but release.ps1 aborts on the PS5.1 git stderr-wrap, stranding completed work uncommitted/unpushed across repos (found real stranded work in 8 repos on 2026-07-27).
items.title: Harden every push-to-github.ps1 against the PS5.1 git stderr-wrap (Invoke-Git guard)
items.prompt: Harden every project's scripts/push-to-github.ps1 (and any release.ps1 that calls git directly) against the PowerShell 5.1 stderr-wrap: git writes benign 'LF will be replaced by CRLF' and 'To https://...' lines to stderr, which PS 5.1 under $ErrorActionPreference='Stop' promotes to a terminating NativeCommandError, aborting the release AFTER committing but BEFORE the push completes and stranding completed work in the working tree. Apply the git-guard.ps1 Invoke-Git wrapper already used by YesAndBudget (relax EAP to Continue around each git call, check $LASTEXITCODE instead of trapping stderr; see memory yab-dashboard-push-warn-false-alarm). Repos to verify/fix: YesAndEverything, YesAndChains, HereBeHordes, BrackishRising, YesAndRing, YesAndCattery, YesAndGnosis, YesAndScheduler, YesAndAgents, YesAndApothecary (Budget already has it). For each: adapt git-guard.ps1, route git add/commit/push through Invoke-Git, then TEST with a trivial doc change through release.ps1 end-to-end and confirm the push lands (git log --oneline @{u}..HEAD empty) with NO Bash fallback. Removes the need for the ship-and-verify Bash workaround now baked into the burndown/drain routines.
items.notes: Root cause of the 2026-07-27 mass-stranding incident. Routine-level ship-and-verify gate is the interim mitigation; this is the real fix.

items.title: GitHub repo description still sells the retired 2D game ("Hand-painted, true 2:1 isometric") against native-3D framing in README, project.godot and CLAUDE.md
items.evidence: First audit pass to walk Phase 5 repo-level metadata; the three prior passes listed it under 'Couldn't verify'. `gh repo view --json description` on TheProphetKane/here-be-hordes returns: "Exoplanet colony defense RTS in Godot 4.6. Portal-anchored outpost extracting resources for a depleted Earth while the native undead refuse to stay buried. Hand-painted, true 2:1 isometric." Both closing claims are pre-v0.98.5 framing. Every other one-line pitch in the project ends the opposite way: project.godot config/description and README.md:3 both close on 'rendered in native 3D from a classic 2:1 overhead view', and CLAUDE.md:8 says 'native 3D with a fixed 2:1-dimetric camera'. CLAUDE.md:21 explicitly tags the wording as historical: 'The retired 2D path was true 2:1 isometric at 32x16 tiles. [legacy-2D]'. So the handler marks the exact phrase as legacy while the repo's one-line pitch still leads with it. Severity is medium rather than high because the repo is confirmed private (isPrivate: true), so nobody outside the project reads it today, but this is the field that becomes the pitch the moment the repo flips public or gets linked, and the field a new collaborator reads before opening the GDD. Verified correct in the same call: homepageUrl is https://yesandeverything.com/hordes/, matching README.md:15. Topics are reasonable for the genre; the 'isometric' topic is defensible since the 3D camera keeps the 2:1 read, and the absence of a '3d' topic is a soft gap rather than a defect. Pattern note: the same v0.99.40 commit band that corrected README.md, CLAUDE.md and docs/ASSET_PROVENANCE.md for the asset purge did not touch this, which matches the policy-lag pattern the 2026-07-27 audit identified for the Locked Decision cards, extended to a surface that lives outside the repo tree entirely.
items.prompt: Update the Here Be Hordes GitHub repo description so it stops describing the retired 2D renderer. Repo: TheProphetKane/here-be-hordes (private). Current description ends 'Hand-painted, true 2:1 isometric.', which CLAUDE.md:21 tags [legacy-2D]; the native-3D rework completed at v0.98.5. Align the closing sentence with the framing README.md:3 and project.godot config/description already use. Suggested full replacement: "Exoplanet colony defense RTS in Godot 4.6. Portal-anchored outpost extracting resources for a depleted Earth while the native undead refuse to stay buried. Grim-dark horror rendered in native 3D from a classic 2:1 overhead view." Apply with: gh repo edit TheProphetKane/here-be-hordes --description "<text>". Optionally add a '3d' topic with --add-topic 3d. This is a change to remote repo settings rather than a working-file edit, so confirm the exact wording with Nick before running it. No version bump and no release script needed; nothing in the working tree changes. Leave homepageUrl alone, it is already correct.
items.notes: Queued by the 2026-07-28 nightly canonical audit. items.title: Skylight can create a mis-owned event but has no way to correct one
items.detail: X:\YesAndSkylight has no way to correct an event filed to the wrong person, and mis-filings are designed in rather than accidental. src/owners.ts:59-65 inferOwner() deliberately falls back to owner=family when it cannot infer one from an inbound email subject/body, and DESIGN.md D14 accepts that trade-off explicitly (a shared event shown to everyone beats one silently filed to a person). So the email front door will keep producing events on the family calendar that belong to Nick or Lexi. Nothing in the project can move them: src/google.ts exports only createEvent() and probe() -- no move, update or delete; DESIGN.md section 6 has no corrective route (POST /api/quick-add only creates); src/ui.ts is a create-only form. Evidence that this bites in practice: commit c2fc67d records that 'Project ChainGrip Pure' (13 Aug) was sitting on the family calendar, is Nick's, and had to be moved to the Nick calendar on 2026-07-25 by hand via Google's events.move API, run outside this Worker. The limitation is now documented in DESIGN.md section 8 (applied by the 2026-07-28 drift-fix pass); this item is the capability itself. Deciding WHICH surface gets it is the structural part: (a) a POST /api/reassign route taking an event id + new owner and calling events.move, (b) a control in the PWA, or (c) no code at all -- just a documented events.move curl recipe in README.md. Option (c) is the cheapest and may be sufficient for a family tool. Whichever is chosen, note the wall's badge letter follows the Skylight profile the destination calendar maps to, so a move fixes the badge too.

items.impact: Every mis-filed event needs a manual trip to Google Calendar or a hand-rolled API call. The email front door guarantees these recur, so the manual work is ongoing rather than one-off.
items.drainNote: Needs an attended pass: choosing between an API route, a UI control, or a documented events.move recipe is a design call on a repo a parallel session owns. Do not add a write path unattended.

items.title: 236 questions marked (secret) render in full, marker and all, on 121 public entity pages
items.detail:
PROJECT_SPEC.md section 6 routeQuestion rule 3 sends a question the DM marked (secret) to /questions-dm, and the same section's stated reason for that page is that players never see it. The routing works: 0 of the 357 public questions.json records carry the marker. But the question TEXT is not routed anywhere. It renders inline on its own entity page, and those pages are public.

Measured 2026-07-28 against a fresh build: 236 (secret)-marked question lines sit on non-secret vault entities, and web/dist renders the literal string '(secret)' 274 times across 121 public pages. Worst offenders: /lore/the-coiled-guardian 14, /locations/mithralholm 12, /locations/cinderfall 8, /locations/ovicor 8, /locations/brasshollow 7, /locations/the-coldwood-march 7, /lore/the-aestral-reckoning 7.

Concrete example, fully readable on /locations/mithralholm without the DM cookie: 'Are the eggs chromatic (evil-blooded) hatching among metallic dragons, and what does the Hoard do about them? (secret)'

Two problems that want different answers.

ONE, the routing is defeated. Marking a question (secret) moves it off the player board but not off the player-visible web. Either the marker should also suppress the question from the public entity render, or section 6 should stop describing the DM queue as content players never see and say plainly that the marker is a board-sorting device only.

TWO, the authoring marker leaks into rendered prose. Even if the question stays public, (secret) is build-time routing syntax, not world prose. The sibling markers do not leak: (dm) and (player) appear 0 times in the built site. This half is a rendering defect on its own terms and is cheap to fix in the question harvester in web/build.mjs.

Severity medium, not high: the affected questions live on entities Kane deliberately left public and no secret: true entity content is exposed, so this is an intent-versus-implementation gap in the spec rather than a live spoiler leak.
items.impact: correctness
items.notes: Intent-versus-implementation gap, not a live leak of secret: true content. Part two (strip the raw marker from rendered prose) is mechanical; part one needs Kane.

items.title: 689 public-page question chips link to /questions-dm, which is a 401 dead end for players
items.detail:
Every answered-question chip on a public entity page links to /questions-dm#q-<qid> with the title 'See this on the questions page'. That path is in web/dm-paths.mjs, so the worker 401s it for anyone without the DM cookie.

Measured 2026-07-28: 689 such links across 215 public built pages. That is 97 percent of all public-to-gated links on the site (712 total); the other 23 are the DM-badged type-index rows and the blessed Maevyn transcript exemption, both sanctioned by the section 6 locked decision.

No content leaks. The target 401s and the chip label is just the word 'answered', so this is a UX defect rather than a security one. It is filed separately from the (secret)-marked-questions item because this half is mechanical where that one is a design call.

The fix is to route the chip to /questions when the question landed on the player board and to render the chip unlinked when routeQuestion sent it to the DM queue, so a player never clicks through to a 401.
items.impact: usability
items.notes: Pure UX. Target 401s so nothing leaks. Mechanical fix, no Kane decision needed.

items.title: The globe cutter leaves orphaned island textures on disk when the island set is re-cut
items.detail:
web/assets/globe/titanoros-i24.webp and titanoros-i24-labels.webp sit on disk unreferenced. web/build.mjs and tools/globe/audit_globe.py both run i1 through i23; disk carries i1 through i24.

This pair has now been in three states across three days: orphaned on 2026-07-26, live again on 2026-07-27 (which is why the queued deletion filed on the 26th was correctly killed as destructive before it could run), and orphaned again on 2026-07-28 after the island set was re-cut.

The two files are about 99 KB together, so the disk cost is nothing. The real finding is the pattern: while the cutter is under active iteration, any queue item naming specific generated assets rots into a destructive instruction within a day. THIS ITEM IS NOT A REQUEST TO DELETE THOSE TWO FILES. Deleting a texture that the next re-cut promotes back into use breaks the globe, which is exactly the trap the 2026-07-26 item set.

The durable fix belongs in the cutter itself: after it writes its patch set, it should reconcile web/assets/globe/ against the indices it just emitted and clean up or report what is left over, so the orphan can never outlive the run that created it.
items.impact: maintainability
items.notes: Explicitly NOT a deletion request. The 2026-07-26 version of this item had to be killed because it named specific files that came back into use. Fix the cutter, not the symptom.

items.title: Agents: the dashboard's only usage metric counts archived receipts and excludes the hourly auth probe, hiding most of the sessions the tool spawns
items.evidence: status/data/Agents.json carries metrics: [{k: 'runs archived', v: '13'}], computed from runs/. probeAuth (server.mjs:121-150) writes no receipt, so no probe lands there. Server up since the 2026-07-20T19:22 relaunch (logs/watchdog.log) at AUTH_CHECK_MS = 1h is roughly 190 probe sessions against 13 archived receipts, only two of which are newer than 2026-07-16.
items.prompt: Agents MEDIUM (bar-raise 2026-07-28): the only usage number Agents publishes is the dashboard metric 'runs archived', computed from the runs/ directory, and it currently reads 13. The hourly headless-auth probe (probeAuth, server.mjs:121-150) deliberately writes no receipt, so none of its sessions appear in that count. Since the last watchdog relaunch on 2026-07-20T19:22 the server has been up continuously, which at AUTH_CHECK_MS of one hour is roughly 190 probe sessions against those 13 receipts, and only two of the receipts are newer than 2026-07-16. The published cost signal therefore understates sessions spawned by more than an order of magnitude, and it understates it in the exact direction that hides the related finding bar-raise-2026-07-24-agents-auth-probe-context-cost (each probe loads the full repo context). Not a request to archive probe receipts, which would bloat runs/ for no diagnostic value. Fix: count probe invocations in the server (a simple counter, plus a cumulative total folded into logs/watchdog-heartbeat.json by the existing heartbeat path), then have scripts/write-dashboard-status.ps1 emit a second metrics row such as {k: 'probe runs', v: '<n>'} alongside 'runs archived'. That makes the credit the tool draws on its own behalf visible next to the work it does on Kane's, without touching the probe itself, which the 2026-07-25 auth incident proved earns its place.
